The project to complete the water transfer ring between Shiraz drinking water reservoirs, one of the most important development programs of the metropolis’s Water and Sewerage Company, has now produced tangible results, permanently resolving water stress in the south, the old urban fabric, and parts of central and eastern Shiraz and fully improving water supply there.
To address water supply problems in Shiraz, significant water projects have been implemented over the past two years, most importantly completing the water supply ring. The plan aims to provide sustainable water across Shiraz by transferring water from the second line of Doroudzan Dam to southern and eastern Shiraz. About 30% of the city’s water production is now supplied from the dam’s second water supply line.
The energy minister and Fars governor also visited Fasa’s wastewater treatment plant, described as a flagship national wastewater project.
According to IRNA, the project to build collection, transmission, and treatment facilities in Fasa, with 135 km of collection network and transmission lines and enabling more than 112,000 people to benefit from modern wastewater services, has become one of Fars Province’s most notable infrastructure and environmental projects.
The Fasa project, which has nearly 80% physical progress in 16 months, is being implemented to improve health indicators, protect water resources, expand use of treated wastewater, and complete urban infrastructure, and ranks among the country’s flagship wastewater projects in terms of speed.

Raheem Sterling pleads guilty to dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
13:35:20 UTC
22:35:20 KST

Raheem Sterling pleaded guilty to dangerous driving and could be sent to prison after driving his Lamborghini for more than an hour on motorways during rush hour while inhaling nitrous oxide.
The former Chelsea and Manchester City forward stood in the dock to accept three charges before Basingstoke magistrates court heard how he embarked on a prolonged period of reckless driving on the M25 and M3, inhaling nitrous oxide balloons, before crashing his £270,000 car. Sterling was disqualified from driving and bailed until 25 November, when his sentence will either be determined or referred to the crown court.
Sterling also admitted possession of nitrous oxide and refusing to provide a specimen.
The maximum term for Sterling would be two years in prison, although a sentence of 12 to 18 months is considered more likely and, with mitigation, that could be suspended.
Simon Jones, prosecuting, told the court one witness had “genuine concerns the driver might kill someone” and described Sterling’s driving as “absolutely horrendous”.
“As she moved past the vehicle she thought the airbag had been deployed, it was a large white deflated balloon,” Jones said. “She had no idea if the driver could see ahead.”
Between 7.45am and 8.52am on 28 May, police received multiple calls reporting dangerous driving – shortly after Sterling had returned to England after a loan at Feyenoord, where he had attempted to revive his career.
Dashcam footage provided to police by one witness showed Sterling’s car swerving between lanes and almost colliding with the central reservation. Witnesses reported seeing the driver inhaling balloons while driving.
After leaving the M3, the Lamborghini veered off the carriageway on the A327 near the Minley interchange in Hampshire. All four tyres blew out and there was damage to the bodywork. Body-worn footage from officers attending the scene, played in court, showed Sterling, 31, sitting in the passenger seat with two canisters on his lap before confirming he had been driving.
Jones said Sterling appeared keen to move a deflated balloon from beside him on to the back seat. His saliva was tested and no presence of cannabis or cocaine was found, but he later refused to provide a blood sample to test for other substances.
Another witness told police they had seen the Lamborghini driving erratically at 1.10am. They reported it entering a drive-through at “alarming speed”, Jones said, and saw the driver holding an inflated balloon.
After his arrest, Sterling was taken to Basingstoke investigation centre. “During the process he had disclosed to staff that he had a problem with nitrous oxide,” Jones said.
Sterling failed a series of impairment tests, including walking in a straight line without swaying and placing his fingertip on the end of his nose. He was also asked to judge 30 seconds with his eyes closed but recorded 52.
Jones said Sterling “appeared to be quiet, withdrawn and lethargic and actively fidgeting” during the tests. “His eyelids were drooping, consistent with fatigue or drug impairment. He said he was feeling very cold, despite this being in the middle of a heatwave with 33-degree temperatures.”
The former England international, who won 82 caps between 2012 and 2022 and played in five major tournaments, was taken to a medical room where he refused to provide a blood sample without providing a reasonable excuse and despite repeated and clear warnings.
At 5.13pm, Sterling was interviewed with a legal representative present. A signed, prepared statement was read out in which he said he had not slept all night and was tired and confused. He then answered “no comment” to officers’ questions.
Jason Bartfield KC for the defence did not dispute this was a top-category case, given the prolonged driving and clear serious impairment. Bartfield cautioned, however, that there would have been “short periods” of “serious impairment”, compared with consuming cannabis or alcohol.
Bartfield did not accept the car damage was serious, describing it as “relatively superficial” and “minor scratching” alongside the blown tyres. He also argued that the fact there were two canisters in Sterling’s lap when police arrived showed “this was very much not a case of trying to conceal anything from them”.
The court was not told the full mitigating circumstances, but Bartfield said: “Clearly there is extensive personal mitigation. Voluntary steps have been taken to address them. I hope this has weight with the court.”
District judge Kirsty Allman ordered a pre-sentence report and adjourned the hearing. She said she had not decided whether to retain jurisdiction or commit sentencing to the crown court. A magistrates court cannot impose a sentence of more than 12 months.
“I’m going to release you on unconditional bail,” she said. “If you don’t attend, a warrant will be issued for your arrest. I’m going to disqualify you from driving as of today. You must not drive a motor vehicle on the road as of today. I will determine the period if I sentence you, otherwise it will be for the crown court. You must not drive while disqualified – if you drive while disqualified you will be committing a prisonable offence.”

Rich countries face Covid-related costs for 20 more years, says OECD
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
13:35:20 UTC
22:35:20 KST

The health and economic impacts from Covid-19 will likely continue for another two decades, according to a report out Tuesday from the world’s wealthiest countries.
The pandemic saw rates of smoking, drinking alcohol and unhealthy eating rise, while care for people with chronic diseases was interrupted. All of which continues to add pressure to today's economies and health systems, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development said in its report.
And while countries continue to feel the squeeze on their budgets from Covid, they also face a one-in-two chance of another pandemic of a similar scale over the next 25 years.
Advertisement
The document, which examines the economic case for pandemic preparedness and response, outlines why early intervention is necessary to avert the worst health and economic impacts.
Nearly 7 million people died from Covid from 2020 to May 2023, while the global economy contracted nearly 4% in 2020 compared to the previous year — a decline comparable to the 2008 global financial crisis, the report said.
The authors modeled outbreaks of viruses similar to Ebola, avian influenza, influenza A, coronavirus and measles to stress test health systems and economies.
Without treatments or vaccines, 1% of the population could die from a coronavirus-like outbreak and more than 5% for an influenza A-like outbreak in the first nine months.
Meanwhile, GDP would shrink by 2.7% during a coronavirus-like outbreak, but could drop 16.2% in the case of an outbreak of a virus similar to measles.
“Transport and storage, manufacturing, and administrative and support services would consistently be among the hardest-hit sectors of the economy.”
This is why early public health measures like hand-washing, masks and distancing are vital to saving lives and economic activities — reducing the need for more drastic action down the line, the report said.

Probe Into Serbian Ruling Party’s Election Call Center Yields No Progress After Three Years
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
13:34:00 UTC
22:34:00 KST

Reported by
As Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic’s party gears up for elections at the end of October, suspicions of vote-buying in previous election cycles remain unresolved.
Serbian police have failed to question a single person in nearly three years of investigating an alleged vote-buying and illicit campaign finance scheme operated by the ruling Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), opting instead to transfer the case between internal departments, the Center for Investigative Journalism of Serbia (CINS) reported.
The stalled investigation takes on renewed significance as Serbia gears up for snap parliamentary elections on October 25. The political stakes were elevated further Monday evening when President Aleksandar Vučić announced on Pink TV that he will officially resign on September 27. Vučić stated he will address the nation to thank them for their support before entering the campaign as an “ordinary citizen” representing the SNS.
“The only thing I can say is that I faithfully served the citizens of this country, faithfully, diligently, devotedly, and with determination,” Vučić said.
The First Basic Public Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade confirmed to CINS that, as of late August, the Ministry of Interior (MUP) had not interviewed anyone regarding the SNS call center case.
Prosecutors initially instructed police to investigate in December 2023 and sent three subsequent reminders, which went unanswered. Instead, on July 8, the MUP transferred the case from its economic crime department to its anti-corruption department. The MUP told CINS it will submit a report to prosecutors once its checks are complete.
The investigation stems from a November 2023 CINS undercover exposé of an SNS call center. A reporter documented that employment was conditional on voting for the ruling party and photographing the ballot as proof. Workers were allegedly organized by the hostess agency M&J Lady and received undeclared cash payments at the offices of a youth non-governmental organization, the Center for Education and Youth Development of Belgrade (CEROB).
The SNS, M&J Lady, and CEROB have all officially denied involvement to Serbia’s Anti-Corruption Agency. Despite the denials, the CINS investigation was cited in the final election report by the OSCE Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights (ODIHR) as an example of voter pressure and illicit third-party campaign financing.
Following the exposé, former opposition Members of Parliament Jelena Jerinić and Đorđe Pavićević filed criminal complaints alleging voting bribery, tax offenses, and unauthorized personal data collection. The case was briefly elevated to the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade but was returned in early 2024 due to alleged insufficient evidence.
Experts have sharply criticized the prolonged delays. Nemanja Nenadić of Transparency Serbia called it one of the country's best-documented campaign finance violations, criticizing prosecutors for failing to direct the investigation or take action when police stalled. Retired police inspector Siniša Janković warned the police's inaction could constitute a criminal offense of abuse of office.
Vladimir Tupanjac, a lawyer and former deputy prosecutor, noted that prosecutors legally did not have to wait for the police and could have gathered the evidence themselves.
"Based on the conduct so far, one could conclude that the police and the prosecution are accomplices in covering up a crime," Tupanjac told CINS.

JASDF Global Hawk Presumed to Have Crashed off Western Japan
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
13:33:00 UTC
22:33:00 KST

A Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF) RQ-4B Global Hawk is presumed to have crashed into the Sea of Japan (East Sea) on September 15 after experiencing communication problems and disappearing from radar. It’s the first such incident involving a JASDF Global Hawk, a high-altitude, unmanned surveillance aircraft manufactured by U.S. defense firm Northrop Grumman.
The aircraft, assigned to the 502nd Squadron of the Airborne Warning and Control Wing at Misawa Air Base in Aomori Prefecture, took off from the base at around 10:20 a.m., according to the JASDF.
Problems connecting with the aircraft’s communications equipment began after 12:55 p.m. Three minutes later, at around 12:58 p.m., its radar track disappeared over waters about 50 kilometers north of Tottori Prefecture in western Japan.
Japan immediately mounted a search for the missing UAV. The effort involved two F-15J fighters, a U-125A search-and-rescue aircraft, a UH-60J helicopter, and a KC-46A tanker from the JASDF, as well as the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force frigate Agano and missile boat Hayabusa.
The Japan Coast Guard discovered floating debris at around 2:19 p.m., and a JASDF F-15J fighter reported a debris sighting six minutes later. The U-125A search-and-rescue aircraft photographed the debris at 3:12 p.m. By 5:20 p.m., the JASDF had determined from the photographs that the debris was likely from the missing Global Hawk.
“Based on the floating objects discovered, the aircraft is presumed to have crashed,” the Air Staff Office said in its second report on the incident.
The cause remains under investigation. No damage outside the Self-Defense Forces had been reported as of 5 p.m.
The incident raises questions not only about what caused the Global Hawk to go down but also about the potential impact on Japan’s intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities.
At a press conference earlier on September 15, JASDF Chief of Staff General Morita Takehiro said the aircraft “was not on a training flight,” but declined to disclose what it had been doing.
Asked by this author whether the Global Hawk was likely to have crashed, Morita said at the time that the JASDF was considering “all possibilities” as it conducted the search. The subsequent discovery of debris led the service to presume that the aircraft had indeed crashed.
The JASDF operates three RQ-4Bs, all based at Misawa. Morita said this was the first time a JASDF Global Hawk had gone missing.
Japan began acquiring the Global Hawk in fiscal year 2015 to strengthen its persistent wide-area surveillance capabilities. The first aircraft arrived at Misawa in March 2022; the third arrived in June 2023, completing the planned three-aircraft fleet.
The RQ-4B is one of the JASDF’s key intelligence-gathering platforms. With a wingspan of about 40 meters and a length of about 15 meters, the UAV can remain airborne for around 36 hours and operate at altitudes of around 60,000 feet. Its high-altitude endurance allows it to monitor vast areas for extended periods without putting an aircrew at risk.
It is also an expensive asset. Japanese Defense Ministry documents put the unit cost of a Global Hawk at approximately 17.3 billion yen ($111.7 million). If the aircraft is ultimately confirmed lost, it would represent not only a significant financial loss but also the loss of one-third of Japan’s small Global Hawk fleet.
Retired JASDF Lt. Gen. Araki Junichi told NHK that a simple loss of communications would not necessarily explain the presumed crash because the aircraft is programmed to return to base if communications are lost. He suggested that an engine or other mechanical problem may have prevented normal flight, although the cause has yet to be established.
Araki also warned that losing one of the three aircraft could make continuous surveillance operations more difficult, potentially requiring other aircraft to compensate and increasing the burden on operational units.
The immediate priority is to recover as much of the aircraft as possible and determine what happened during the critical three-minute period between the onset of communication problems and the disappearance of its radar track.
Investigators will also need to establish what the aircraft was doing at the time, why communications failed, whether its automatic return-to-base function was activated, and why the aircraft was apparently unable to continue flying or return to base.
The answers will be important not only for preventing a recurrence, but also for assessing the reliability of a strategically important surveillance capability at a time when Japan is seeking to strengthen persistent intelligence-gathering around its increasingly contested neighborhood.

Lebanon’s economic losses from Israel’s wars since 2023 could exceed $27 billion, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam has said, warning that reconstruction is beyond the state’s current capacity and will require Arab and international funding.
Salam made the remarks on Tuesday during a general debate on government policies in parliament, saying the scale of destruction had outstripped the country’s resources.
“We must also be frank with the Lebanese people: the scale of destruction is far greater than the state’s capacity,” Salam said.
“Therefore, reconstruction and recovery require, alongside state resources, Arab and international support and major external funding,” he added.
Salam linked securing reconstruction funding to restoring confidence in the state and implementing reforms.
“There can be no sustainable reconstruction without funding, no funding without trust, and no trust without a capable state. Reaching a capable state, of course, requires reform,” he said.
Wars deepen Lebanon’s economic losses
Addressing Israel’s assault on Lebanon, Salam said Beirut “did not choose the war that overtook the country last March”.
“We were not even asked for our opinion about entering it. It was imposed on us at a time when the deep wounds of the 2023-2024 war had not yet healed,” he said.
Salam said the World Bank had estimated the total cost of the first war, which began on October 8 2023, at around $14 billion.
The figure included approximately $7.2 billion in physical damage and $6.8 billion in economic losses caused by disrupted activity and declining production and revenues, he said.
For the latest Israeli assault, which began last March, Salam said the World Bank had estimated the direct cost so far at between $3 billion and $4 billion.
“Therefore, the two wars together have certainly cost Lebanon more than $20 billion, and their total cost may exceed $27 billion once the cost of the 2026 war is fully calculated,” Salam said.
“But these figures do not fully reflect the real cost,” he added.
The prime minister said the estimates did not account for brain drain, lost investments, damage to the education sector, declining land and asset values, or delayed recovery from Lebanon’s financial crisis, which has continued since 2019.
He said preliminary estimates placed the broader economic cost beyond direct physical destruction at between $4 billion and $5 billion.
Lebanon has faced two deadly Israeli assaults since October 2023, causing widespread destruction, major damage to infrastructure and homes, and deepening the country’s economic losses.
On June 26, Beirut and Tel Aviv signed a US-sponsored framework agreement in Washington that provides for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory and the deployment of the Lebanese army in areas vacated by Israeli forces.
Despite the agreement, Israel continues to launch attacks on southern Lebanon and maintains its occupation of areas in the south, some held for decades and others seized during more recent wars and military operations.

Kenya beats European rivals to bring World Athletics Championships to Africa
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
13:32:31 UTC
22:32:31 KST

Kenya beats European rivals to bring World Athletics Championships to Africa
Kenya will host the 2029 World Athletics Championships, becoming the first African country to stage the sport’s flagship global competition.
World Athletics announced on Tuesday that Nairobi has beaten rival bids from London, Rome, and Munich. Munich was instead awarded the 2031 edition, while Beijing will host the championships in 2027.
“Taking our championships to Africa for the first time will be historic,” World Athletics President Sebastian Coe said. He described Nairobi’s bid as “compelling and emotional,” citing Kenya’s prominence in international athletics.
Kenyan President William Ruto welcomed the decision as a victory for the continent. “This is Kenya’s moment, Africa’s moment, and a victory for generations of athletes who made our nation synonymous with excellence on the track, on the road and cross-country,” he said. Ruto pledged that the East African country would deliver “an unforgettable championship worthy of our athletes, our country and our continent.”
The event will be the first senior World Athletics Championships held in either Kenya or anywhere else in Africa. However, the East African country has previously staged several major international competitions. Mombasa hosted the 2007 World Cross Country Championships, while Nairobi staged the World Under-18 Championships in 2017 and the World Under-20 Championships in 2021. The capital also hosted the African Athletics Championships in 2010.
Kenya has produced some of the world’s most successful runners, including Olympic champions Eliud Kipchoge, Faith Kipyegon, David Rudisha, and Kipchoge Keino.
The East African country unsuccessfully sought the 2025 championships, which were awarded to Tokyo. World Athletics President Coe said Nairobi returned with a stronger proposal supported by the ongoing overhaul of Kasarani Stadium. The venue is also being renovated ahead of the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations football tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Tanzania and Uganda.
The award comes as Kenyan athletics continues to face scrutiny over doping. The Athletics Integrity Unit classifies Kenya among the national federations at the highest risk of doping and subjects its athletes to stricter testing requirements.
The decision adds to Africa’s growing list of major international sporting events. Morocco will become the continent’s second country to host matches at a men’s FIFA World Cup when it stages the 2030 tournament with Spain and Portugal. South Africa became the first in 2010. Moroccan officials are also seeking to stage the 2030 final at the planned 115,000-seat Hassan II Stadium near Casablanca, although FIFA has yet to choose the venue.
Senegal will meanwhile host the Youth Olympic Games from October 31 to November 13, 2026. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye formally received the Olympic flame in Dakar on September 12 ahead of the event – the first Olympic sporting competition to be held in Africa.

Obwohl die Bundesrepublik massiv liefert, lähmt die ständige Angst vor Eskalation die strategische Handlungsfähigkeit des Westens. Die entscheidende Frage lautet: Wie lässt sich Wladimir Putin überhaupt noch an den Verhandlungstisch zwingen?
Im Gespräch analysiert Schularick, warum der russische Präsident trotz einer massiv überhitzten Kriegswirtschaft und drohender Bankenkrisen nicht freiwillig einlenken wird.

China's carbon market expands as annual trading volume hits record high
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
21:31:30 CST
22:31:30 KST

WUHAN, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- China's national carbon market had recorded a cumulative trading volume of 961 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent by the end of August 2026, with total turnover reaching 65.7 billion yuan (about 9.71 billion U.S. dollars), according to an ongoing carbon market conference in central China.
In 2025, this market operated for 243 trading days, with annual trading volume hitting a record 235 million tonnes, up 24.36 percent year on year, while transaction value reached 14.63 billion yuan, according to a report released Tuesday at the China Carbon Market Conference 2026 in Wuhan, Hubei Province.
China expanded the market's industry coverage for the first time in 2025. As of 2026, a total of 3,680 key emitters from the power generation, steel, cement and aluminum smelting sectors have been included, covering around 8.3 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions, or more than 65 percent of the national total.
Preparatory work is also underway to bring sectors like petrochemicals, chemicals, papermaking and civil aviation into the market.
China officially launched its national carbon emissions trading market in July 2021, which has since evolved into the world's largest carbon market in terms of total greenhouse gas emissions traded.
China's voluntary greenhouse gas emissions reduction market has also gathered pace. By the end of August, 41 projects had been registered, with cumulative trading volume reaching 21.71 million tonnes and transaction value totaling 1.74 billion yuan.
In March, a mangrove restoration project in Xiapu County of east China's Fujian Province became the first such project to complete registration under the voluntary emissions reduction market, marking a milestone in safeguarding and restoring China's marine ecosystems.
Addressing the conference in Wuhan, Minister of Ecology and Environment Huang Runqiu said China will further strengthen the carbon market's role in cutting emissions, diversify trading products and market participants, and expand international exchanges and cooperation.
China aims to encompass all major industrial sectors in the carbon trading market by 2027, while the national voluntary greenhouse gas emission reduction trading market is expected to expand to include all key fields, according to a guideline unveiled last year.
China has announced the goal of peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality before 2060. ■

World Athletics chief Seb Coe: 'We stand firm against Russian athletes taking part'
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
13:31:25 UTC
22:31:25 KST

Coe rejected Moscow's claims of a 'personal obsession' with banning Russian athletes and reflected on his term and the crisis at FIFA.
In an exclusive interview with Euronews, the President of World Athletics Sebastian Coe defended the organisation's decision to keep Russian athletes barred from its events.
The International Olympic Committee announced in the summer that it was easing the relevant restrictions, but left it to each international sports federation to take its own decisions. Euronews asked whether, in the light of those developments and of decisions taken by other federations, World Athletics plans to change its stance.
Athletics is, after all, the sport often described as "the king of the Olympic Games". Coe's answer, however, leaves no room for misinterpretation: "We will maintain our position and we will defend our position."
The second question concerned the pushback (on a legal basis) in recent months from the Russian side against the hard line taken by World Athletics. Over the summer, the Russian Athletics Federation lodged two appeals against World Athletics at the Court of Arbitration for Sport in Lausanne (CAS), arguing that the decision to maintain the exclusion "affects the fundamental interests of athletics in Russia and restricts the right of Russian athletes to compete."
Just last week, groups of Russian athletes appealed to the human rights commissions of the IOC and the UN, claiming that their exclusion violates their rights and is destroying their careers. Coe's response to this barrage of Russian legal action was, once again: "We will maintain our position and we will defend our position."
'It is not a personal issue but one of philosophy'
This stance, banning Russian (and Belarusian) athletes from all World Athletics competitions, was recently described as "Coe's personal obsession" by the executive director of the Russian Athletics Federation, Boris Yarisevsky.
"It is clear that there is something personal here. I believe this is simply his personal position. It is not the position of World Athletics. The sanctions against the Russian Athletics Federation are unprecedented. No other sports federation is facing such strict restrictions.
They not only prevent smooth day to day operations, they also hold back the development of athletics in Russia, especially among young athletes who cannot represent their country on the international stage.
We are seeking the lifting of the sanctions through the courts and are preparing our next steps to restore justice", Yarisevsky. told Russian media.
Euronews asked Coe, a British Olympic champion who won four medals in Moscow 1980 and Los Angeles in 1984 to respond, and once again he was unequivocal, although this time more verbose: "Fighting for the integrity of competition and the integrity of competitors and the primacy of an international federation to decide how it determines eligibility is not a personal issue, it is one of philosophy."
It should be noted that World Athletics imposed the current sanctions and full exclusion on Russian athletes in March 2022, as an immediate response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
It was the first major sports federation to take such a decision and has kept it in place almost four and a half years later, even though the International Olympic Committee and other federations such as the international wrestling, judo and fencing federations and World Aquatics have already relaxed theirs.
Lesson from the 'Ultimate Championship'
Sebastian Coe spoke to Euronews on the sidelines of the Ultimate Championship, the new World Athletics event staged last weekend in Budapest. He sees the competition as one of the key legacies he will leave to his successors when his term as World Athletics president ends in a year's time.
"I hope it's a very, very strong legacy because we're looking at the sport in a very different way. We want this to feel different, to look different, particularly for the athletes. The prize money is significantly larger than we've ever had before, $10 million. And the format is significantly different because it's not a full world championships with 2,000 athletes. It's 381 from 65 different countries. But it really does determine the best of the best.", Coe said at the outset.
The World Athletics president went on: "I think there are things we're going to learn from this that we're gonna be able to take into our world championships, maybe the Olympic program, around event presentation, around just being more exciting and more innovative in the stadium and what it looks like on television".
The legacy of Coe's 12-year presidency
Coe stood for re-election a year and a half ago, in a process held in Ancient Olympia. Kirsty Coventry ultimately came out on top.
Sebastian Coe will therefore complete his third and final four-year term as president of World Athletics in 2027. The federation's statutes were amended at his initiative in order to avoid presidents staying in office for life, as was sometimes the case in the past.
He took over the leadership of what was then the IAAF (International Association of Athletics Federations) in 2015, after elections held on the sidelines of the World Athletics Championships in Beijing, where, a year from now, his successor at the head of World Athletics will be chosen. The IAAF was renamed World Athletics in 2019.
We asked him for a brief assessment of his most significant achievements. He chose to highlight the following:
"We are now the best governed sport in the Olympic movement, by some distance. All the work that's been done by the ASOIF Governance Review (Association of Summer Olympic International Federations) shows that, and that's not where we started.
We've worked really hard to put governances, safeguards, checks, and balances in place. We have an athletic integrity unit that now has made independent all our drug testing, but also our integrity programs, the way we manage ourselves during elections all that is is very very different
I'm very pleased that we are the only olympic sport that has a gender balance council we have twenty six members thirteen men thirteen women and each and every one of them is there on merit
And that is important and in the last four years we've increased our revenues significantly and people want to invest in our sport. Across a whole series of metrics, we're in much better shape than when I took over".
'No comment' on Infantino and the Olympics
Sebastian Coe has achieved all this at a time when global sports governance appears to be in crisis, as shown by the growing pressure on FIFA president Gianni Infantino to step down from the head of world football's governing body, and by the resignation of Edgar Grospiron, president of the organising committee for the 2030 Winter Olympic Games in the French Alps.
Given that Coe is himself the president of what he calls "the best governed" sport federation, and also served as president of the London 2012 Olympic Games Organising Committee.
When asked for his view, he provided a diplomatic answer: "I'm not really interested in other sports and I'm not really interesting in other organising committees. My responsibility is to chair the boards at World Athletics and I am satisfied that not only have we come a long way in improving our governance, we are the best governed sport in the world and I have a council that is accountable and responsible and those are the foundation stones for a very promising future.", Coe replied.
"So, could everyone learn from you?" we asked, picking up on his remark. Coe, smiling, was quick to reply: "I'm not even saying that, I'm just saying that we've done what we have done in the best interests of our sport and that is the only way to manage an organisation."

Indonesia's external debt rises slightly to 454.8 bln USD in July
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
21:31:05 CST
22:31:05 KST

JAKARTA, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- Indonesia's external debt edged up to 454.8 billion U.S. dollars in July from 454.5 billion dollars in June, Bank Indonesia said Tuesday.
On a year-on-year basis, the country's external debt grew 4.9 percent, mainly driven by an increase in public-sector external debt amid a decline in private-sector debt, said Ramdan Denny Prakoso, executive director of Bank Indonesia's Communications Department.
Government external debt stood at 218.4 billion dollars, up 3.2 percent year on year, mainly due to inflows into international government securities. The debt was used to support sectors including health, government administration, education, construction and transportation.
Meanwhile, private-sector external debt fell 1.2 percent year on year to 194.5 billion dollars, with the largest shares coming from the manufacturing, financial services and insurance, electricity and gas, and mining sectors.
Bank Indonesia said the country's external debt structure remained healthy, with the external debt-to-gross domestic product ratio at 30.7 percent and long-term debt accounting for the majority of the total. ■

JAKARTA, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- Indonesian authorities are considering raising a ferry that sank in the Java Sea as search operations continued Tuesday for 129 people still missing among the 243 people aboard.

Search teams were operating across six sectors, which could be adjusted based on updated information, authorities said.
The ferry lost contact early Sunday in waters off Masalembo while sailing from Surabaya to Banjarmasin. ■

Thailand's eastern industrial hub eyes deeper economic ties with China to boost sustainable growth
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
21:31:00 CST
22:31:00 KST

RAYONG, Thailand, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- Thailand's eastern industrial powerhouse of Rayong is positioning itself alongside neighboring Chonburi province as the premier destination for Chinese high-tech manufacturing, electric vehicles (EVs), and digital infrastructure within the country's Eastern Economic Corridor.
Speaking at a recent investment seminar attended by public officials and business leaders, Rayong Governor Traiphop Wongtrairat framed the current influx of Chinese capital as an extension of centuries-old historical ties, encouraging Chinese enterprises to view the province as a long-term partner for sustainable economic growth.
To secure long-term bilateral supply chains, Traiphop highlighted major multi-modal infrastructure projects advancing across the seaboard, including expansions at Rayong's Map Ta Phut deep-sea port and Chonburi's Laem Chabang port.
Aviation logistics are also being upgraded, with developments at U-Tapao International Airport aimed at matching the capacity of Bangkok's Suvarnabhumi Airport through 24-hour flight operations, he said.
Traiphop underscored that Chinese investment is already a primary driver of the local economy. In the Thai-Chinese Rayong Industrial Zone alone, enterprises currently employ nearly 70,000 Thai workers.
Rayong now boasts the highest per capita income in Thailand, heavily anchored by a rapidly clustering Chinese manufacturing presence that includes major EV automakers such as BYD, Changan, and Chery, alongside battery, electronics, and auto-parts suppliers, he added.
To ensure sustainable foreign investments, the governor called on investors to adhere to local standards and work closely with authorities on building permits, zoning, and localized environmental monitoring for air, noise, and wastewater pollution.
The seminar, co-organized last Friday by the sustainable Thailand-China business coordination and promotion mechanism, called for closer collaboration between the public and private sectors to navigate regulatory frameworks and secure long-term growth.
During a group interview, Viboon Supakarapongkul, vice chairman of the Thai Chamber of Commerce, pointed to the expanding economic partnership between Thailand and China.
Viboon said Chinese investment inflows into Thailand have accelerated significantly over the past few years, underpinned by deep-rooted cultural and trade ties, robust local supply chains, and strong bilateral communication that helps investors navigate the regional market.
Technology and advanced manufacturing have emerged as the fastest-growing drivers of this investment wave. Viboon stressed that this influx goes beyond immediate manufacturing capacity, providing critical opportunities for knowledge and technology transfer to the local workforce.
By adopting and mastering these technologies, Thai industries can accelerate domestic capacity building and boost long-term competitiveness, he added.
Viboon affirmed that while private sector organizations stand ready to facilitate partnerships and build investor confidence, sustainable growth depends on clear policy direction from state authorities and an alignment of mutual interests.
Meaningful, lasting investment must deliver concrete advantages for the host country, foster tangible benefits for local communities through employment and shared prosperity, and generate viable returns for investors, he said. ■

China requires online hotel booking platforms to maintain healthy market environment
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
21:30:47 CST
22:30:47 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- Chinese online hotel booking platform companies are required to take primary responsibility for compliance, must prevent and defuse industry competition risks, and maintain a healthy and orderly tourism market environment.
This requirement was announced at a joint administrative guidance meeting for the online hotel booking platform service industry held by the State Administration for Market Regulation and the Ministry of Culture and Tourism on Tuesday.
The meeting noted that fair competition is the cornerstone of the rule of law in the market economy, while compliant operation is the lifeline of enterprise development.
In recent years, China's online hotel booking platform service industry has developed rapidly, playing a positive role in making people's lives more convenient and boosting tourism consumption.
However, competition risks cannot be ignored. As key players in the industry, online hotel booking platform companies should stay within the bounds of the law, uphold fair competition, strengthen compliance management, and promote the healthy development of the industry.
The meeting required platform companies to comply with relevant laws and regulations, learn from cases, conduct self-examinations, and prevent and defuse the risks of "involution-style" competition.
Platform companies should enhance compliance awareness, improve long-term compliance mechanisms, and foster a market order featuring quality products, fair prices and healthy competition.
They should also safeguard consumers' lawful rights and interests and promote win-win outcomes across the platform ecosystem, the meeting said.
The meeting came amid intensifying regulatory scrutiny of the online travel sector.
In July, the State Administration for Market Regulation penalized Trip.com Group for abusing its market dominance, confiscating 1.658 billion yuan (about 245 million U.S. dollars) in illegal gains and imposing a 3.521-billion-yuan fine, equivalent to 7.5 percent of its sales in China in 2025. These two amounts total 5.179 billion yuan.
Separately, Trip.com, China's largest online travel platform, was ordered to refund roughly 122 million yuan in booking deposits withheld from hotels.
China's online accommodation market was valued at approximately 34 billion U.S. dollars in 2025 and is projected to reach nearly 65 billion dollars by 2031, according to a report by Mordor Intelligence, an industry analysis and consulting company.
By the end of 2025, the number of online travel booking users in China had reached 515 million, accounting for 45.8 percent of all internet users in the country. ■

Philippines' claim of so-called maritime jurisdiction over China's territory is illegal: spokesperson
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
21:30:37 CST
22:30:37 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Tuesday that the Philippines' claim of so-called maritime jurisdiction over China's territory is illegal.
Guo made the remarks at a regular press briefing, adding that China will continue to take resolute measures to safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests, and firmly oppose any infringement.
It is reported that in a statement issued on Sept. 11, the Philippines' Department of Foreign Affairs reaffirmed the Philippines' sovereign rights and jurisdiction over Meiji Jiao and Zhubi Jiao as low-tide elevations (LTE) within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone and continental shelf. Later, it changed the narrative, reaffirming its sovereignty over Zhubi Jiao as an LTE within the territorial sea of Zhongye Dao.
"Nansha Qundao, including Meiji Jiao, Zhubi Jiao and Zhongye Dao, are China's inherent territory. It is totally legitimate and lawful for China to conduct construction and other activities on its own territory, a matter within China's sovereignty," Guo said.
He said the territorial scope of the Philippines has already been defined by a series of international treaties. Nansha Qundao has never been part of the Philippine territory, Guo stressed.
"According to the 'land dominates the sea' principle in international law, the Philippines' claim of so-called maritime jurisdiction over China's territory is illegal," said Guo, adding the Philippine side at one point claimed that Zhubi Jiao is within its exclusive economic zone (EEZ) and continental shelf, but later claimed that it lies within the territorial sea of the island it illegally occupies.
"This only exposes how absurd and random its claim is, making it totally untenable," the spokesperson noted.
He said the "South China Sea arbitration" is completely a political manipulation by the Philippines to grab unlawful gains. The so-called "award" is illegal, null and void, and has no binding force, Guo added.
Noting the Philippines' so-called "Maritime Zones Act" illegally includes China's Huangyan Dao and most of the islands and reefs in Nansha Qundao and relevant waters into the Philippines' maritime zone, Guo said this is a grave violation of China's territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests in the South China Sea, and is illegal and null and void.
"China firmly opposes it and will never accept it," said Guo, adding the Philippines should immediately stop infringing upon China's rights, and stop the provocations and publicity stunts. ■

CAPE TOWN, Sept. 15 (Xinhua) -- South Africa and the New Development Bank (NDB) have signed a 1-billion-U.S.-dollar loan agreement to upgrade infrastructure and support reforms in the country's metropolitan municipalities, South Africa's National Treasury announced on Tuesday.
The loan will be used to upgrade infrastructure for metropolitan municipal services in South Africa as part of the Metro Trading Services Reform Program (MTSR), the treasury said in a statement.
"The MTSR is a South African government-led reform program aimed at improving the governance, financial sustainability and operational performance of municipal trading services in metropolitan municipalities, particularly in water and sanitation, electricity and energy, and solid waste management," it said.
"This is a performance-based loan with financing linked to institutional strengthening and the achievement of independently verified measurable performance targets, that are approved by metro councils for their trading services," the treasury said.
The NDB is financing the program alongside the World Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, KFW Development Bank and the French Development Agency, according to the statement.
The NDB loan has a nominal value of 1 billion U.S. dollars, with a 16-year maturity and a three-year grace period, according to the statement.
The financing forms part of broader government efforts to reform municipal trading services in metropolitan municipalities and improve the sustainability of urban infrastructure, it added.
"National Treasury extends its appreciation to the NDB for its support to this government-led reform toward better services for residents and stronger, more sustainable cities," the statement said.
The NDB is a multilateral development bank established by the original BRICS members -- Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa -- in 2015 to mobilize resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects in emerging markets and developing countries. ■

Iran’s large trade delegation in Russia: an opportunity for a leap in exchanges

Iran’s ambassador to Russia, in remarks at the ceremony, referring to the West’s anti-Iranian measures in the field of sanctions, the imposition of two wars, and the martyrdom of the martyred leader of the Islamic Revolution and other compatriots, said: “The message of each of these martyrdoms is that the Islamic Republic of Iran becomes stronger.”
Kazem Jalali continued by describing the recent remarks of the US president as an admission that military aggression against Iran was not carried out with goals such as supporting the people, freedom, and human rights.
Stating that “We stand by our Iran,” he said: “Iranian traders, who pave the way for the prosperity of the country’s production and exports, have in practice shown their commitment to Iran.”
Iran’s ambassador to Russia, referring to regional and global developments, said: “A valuable opportunity is now available to strengthen trade between Tehran and Moscow, and in this regard, not only must relations between the two countries be strengthened, but ties must be founded that would not be damaged even if the current situation in international relations changes.”
He cited the strengthening and full launch of the North-South Corridor capacity, as well as the transfer of Russian gas to Iran, as projects that will sustain trade relations between the two countries for decades.
Jalali, expressing satisfaction that Iran’s trade office in Russia is being established through the efforts of a private-sector company, expressed hope that this measure will accelerate the development of trade exchanges between the two countries.
Iran will also defeat the enemy’s economic war
Bushehr Governor also said in remarks at the meeting: “After failing in military aggression, the enemy has turned to siege and economic war; although this situation has made trade conditions difficult in the southern coastal provinces of the country, Iran is a great and large country with special capacities, and by relying on these capabilities, the enemy’s new actions will also fail.”
Arsalan Zare, emphasizing the importance of the role of the diplomatic apparatus in supplying the country’s needs for essential goods, described the efforts of Iran’s embassy in Russia in this regard as valuable and worthy of appreciation.
In another part of his remarks, stating that Bushehr Province enjoys unparalleled capacities for attracting investment, he referred to this province as Iran’s economic and energy capital and said: “Despite having 1.5 percent of Iran’s area and population, this province has an 8 percent share in the country’s GDP, and this situation has made Bushehr a favorable province for economic activities and investment.”
Yazd Governor also said in remarks at the meeting that the presence of the province’s delegation in Russia is in line with strengthening provincial diplomacy, and described this approach of the country’s foreign policy apparatus as a valuable initiative.
Mohammad Reza Babaei, referring to the production capabilities and capacities in Yazd Province, noted: “More than 900 types of goods are produced in this province, some of which are produced beyond national needs and for export.”
He described Yazd Province’s capability in producing 140 materials needed in the construction industry, as well as producing greenhouse products, as an opportunity for developing the province’s exports to other countries, including Russia.
Meeting Russia’s needs is an opportunity for the country’s economy
Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Head of Iran’s Fisheries Organization also said in remarks at the meeting, referring to the emphasis of the martyred leader of the Islamic Revolution and also our country’s president on developing relations with Russia: “Tehran and Moscow are considered trustworthy friends for each other, and Iranian traders playing a role in meeting Russia’s needs will be an opportunity to support our country’s production and economy.”
Hamzeh Rostamipour added: “If we want sustainable trade relations with Russia, we must witness the prominent role of the private sector, just as today in the fisheries sector, non-governmental sector actors are pioneers and have high returns in fisheries and aquatic production.”
He noted: “The presence of more than 300 Iranian traders from various provinces at the two international exhibitions in Russia, as well as the presence of our country’s pavilion (integrated national pavilion) at the International Fisheries and Aquaculture Exhibition in St. Petersburg, shows that actors in the field of production and economy have come to the field for Iran.”
Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Head of the country’s Veterinary Organization also said in this meeting, referring to the missions of this organization: “As soldiers of the beloved homeland, we are alongside and support you in all stages of production, harvesting, and transportation of products.”
Vahid Salehi, stating that he carries the warm greetings of the Minister of Agriculture-Jihad to Iranian food and fisheries production actors on the trip to Russia, said: “The Supreme Advisory Committee for Resilience and Policy-making in the Field of Food Security has been formed in this ministry.”
He invited production actors to join this committee and present their solutions for elevating the country’s economy.
At this meeting, a number of economic actors presented their issues, views, and proposed solutions for developing trade with Russia, and the officials present at the session responded to the topics raised, which caused the meeting to be prolonged.
A group of economic actors, managers, and members of the chambers of commerce of the provinces of Bushehr, Yazd, Khuzestan, East Azerbaijan, Hormozgan, Sistan and Baluchestan, Chaharmahal and Bakhtiari, Zanjan, Kerman, Fars, Gilan, Golestan, Isfahan, Razavi Khorasan, Tehran, Alborz, Markazi, and Lorestan have traveled to Russia as Iran’s trade delegation.
The Governor of Abadan, a number of deputies and managers of the Fisheries and Veterinary Organizations, the Aquatic Production and Trade Union, and the Greenhouse Growers Association are also present on this trip.
Members of Iran’s large trade delegation on this trip, in addition to participating in the two international exhibitions in Russia, will negotiate with government officials and the private sector of that country about ways to remove obstacles and develop economic cooperation.
According to IRNA, the International Food and Beverage Industry Exhibition of Russia will be held during September 15-18 in Moscow, and the International Fisheries and Aquaculture Exhibition will be held during September 16-18 in St. Petersburg.

South Korea embraces Central Asian leaders, looking to boost regional clout
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
13:30:03 UTC
22:30:03 KST

South Korea embraces Central Asian leaders, looking to boost regional clout
Seoul is set to host its first presidential meeting with five Russia-allied states positioning themselves as a bloc.
South Korea is set to welcome the heads of the five Central Asian states for the first-ever presidential summit between Seoul and the region, a meeting local media have dubbed “historic”.
Wednesday’s summit, preceded by bilateral meetings between South Korean President Lee Jae Myung and leaders of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan, aims to deepen economic engagement between Central Asia and the host, and put them on a more permanent footing.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items
- list 1 of 4Kazakhstan’s Tokayev appoints longtime adviser as vice president
- list 2 of 4Kyrgyzstan hosts pivotal SCO summit amid global geopolitical shifts
- list 3 of 4BRICS meets in India: What’s on the agenda, why it matters
- list 4 of 4South Korean officials decry ‘worst ever’ Asian Games accommodation
“The first expectation is political. The summit will raise a dialogue that has existed since 2007 to the level of heads of state. But the real test is whether it produces a workable agenda in critical minerals, energy, digital technologies and transport,” Sanat Kushkumbayev, from the Kazakhstan Institute for Strategic Studies, told Al Jazeera.
“For Central Asia, the value of the meeting is also in showing that the region can engage external partners collectively without giving up national priorities. I would expect a framework for regular high-level cooperation, followed by more detailed bilateral deals.”
Central Asian states, which are increasingly positioning themselves as a bloc known as C5+, are looking for investments, access to technology and to diversify their international partnerships beyond Moscow and Beijing, analysts said, while South Korea needs to diversify its economic and supply-chain dependencies.
“Currently, South Korea has a limited domestic resource base and a significant supply-chain exposure to China, particularly in critical materials, components and other industrial inputs. Central Asia can offer South Korea critical minerals, energy, alternative production opportunities and greater supply chain diversification. Korea, in return, can provide technology, capital and industrial expertise,” said Sabina Insebayeva, a political scientist at Nazarbayev University.
She explained that the K-Silk Road initiative, South Korea’s strategy for Central Asia launched in 2024, aims to go beyond securing raw materials to develop processing, manufacturing and technology capacity in partnership with local companies.
Central Asia no longer wants to position itself as an exporter of raw materials. Instead, it is seeking the skills and technology needed for domestic industrial hubs. South Korea can act as a long-term partner to achieve this goal, particularly in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
“Kazakhstan already accounts for much of South Korea’s trade and investment presence in the region, so it can reasonably push for larger industrial projects, research facilities and local supplier networks. The difficult part will be moving from assembly and memorandums to genuine localisation and commercial production,” Kushkumbayev explained.
By the end of 2025, the lump-sum volume of South Korea’s direct investment in Central Asia reached about $6.4bn.
But its appeal in Central Asia goes beyond its potential as an investor and technology provider, as a social connection has long been in place.
South Korea’s historical ties to the region
In 1937, at the order of Joseph Stalin, more than 170,000 Soviet Koreans were forcibly relocated from the USSR’s Far East to Soviet Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, under the pretext of preventing Japanese sabotage.
“When my grandparents arrived in southern Kazakhstan, it was autumn, and it was already cold, but they had no houses to live in. That winter they lived with local Kazakh people who supported them and deportees from other countries,” said Roman Zakharov, a half-Korean artist from Kazakhstan.
His grandparents waited for a year to receive housing from the authorities, but as deportees, they had no permission to leave the collective farms they worked on until Stalin’s death.
The deportees and their descendants, collectively called Koryo-saram, have sought to stay connected to their roots, but this has not been easy.
“Koryo-saram tried to adapt local products like carrots to make Korean pickled food. But local Korean culture changed through time … My grandmother tried to listen to South Korean programmes on TV, but she couldn’t understand anything. It was a different language than my grandparents spoke,” said Zakharov, whose art pieces were shown at an exhibition in South Korea in 2023.
When the Soviet Union collapsed, South Korea began founding cultural centres across Central Asia, where local people, including Koryo-saram, could learn the language and engage with Korean culture. Zakharov’s sister attended traditional Korean dance classes.
But the breakthrough for Korean soft power in Central Asia came in the 2010s when soap operas and K-pop became the talk of the town.
“The South Korean government has been popularising Korean culture in Central Asia and using it as a soft power which is already very strong,” said Aiganym Toleuliyeva, a 28-year-old Kazakh researcher, who moved to South Korea to study in 2019.
“In Astana, there is a Korean kimchi festival, and a Korean music festival funded by the Korean embassy. It’s through this kind of soft power and encouraging young people from Central Asia to study in South Korea that Korea is expanding in the region.”
When she first visited Korea in 2015, few locals were familiar with her homeland. But as time went by, the relations grew too.
Today, Central Asia is a tourist destination for South Koreans and for some in the region, Seoul’s appeal extends beyond music, the beauty industry and soap operas.
“Central Asian workers in Korea are also treated better than immigrants in Russia, where the situation is becoming increasingly dangerous,” said Toleuliyeva. “Today Korea offers more opportunities for immigrants from Central Asia; they feel supported. People from Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan – and soon Kazakhstan, too – can join special programmes for labour workers, study the language for free and move to Korea to work on construction sites.”
In a region trying to diversify its partnerships beyond China and Russia, South Korea could be seen as a less politically loaded partner.
“There is a geopolitical element too. Seoul wants a stronger and more visible position in a region where China, Russia, the European Union, Turkiye and the Gulf states are already active,” Kushkumbayev said. “But the Korean approach is likely to remain commercially driven and relatively low-key, rather than openly geopolitical.”

Finland provides Ukraine with €290 million military aid package
Ukrinform reports this, citing the Finnish Ministry of Defence’s official website.
“Finland continues to support Ukraine as it defends itself against Russia’s unlawful aggression. Throughout the war, we have provided Ukraine with materiel assistance based on its needs,” Finnish Minister of Defence Antti Häkkänen said.
The new aid package includes equipment that Ukraine urgently needed. According to the ministry, in terms of value, it is the second-largest package Finland has provided to Ukraine.
According to him, in addition to transferring defense materiel from its own stocks, Finland has purchased products from the Finnish defense industry for Ukraine, some of which are included in this aid package.
“Thus, Finland’s support for Ukraine will also contribute to strengthening the capabilities of our own defense industry,” Häkkänen noted.
The total value of defense materiel provided by Finland to Ukraine has reached €3.6 billion.
The Ministry of Defence emphasized that, for operational security reasons, no further details would be provided regarding the contents of the aid package, its delivery method, or the delivery schedule.
It is also noted that the decision to provide the aid took into account both Ukraine’s needs and the resources available to the Finnish Defence Forces.
As previously reported by Ukrinform, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelensky said that Canada would not only purchase PAC-3 interceptors for Patriot systems for CAD 350 million (approximately USD 270 million), but would also provide AIM-9 and AIM-120 missiles and help purchase the necessary equipment from other countries.

Russia continues systematic attacks aimed at disrupting logistics across Ukraine, Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha said.
“Last night, another locomotive was directly hit in a Russian strike on railway infrastructure near the Polish border in Ukraine’s Volyn oblast. Since the start of the full-scale invasion, over 500 locomotives have been damaged or completely destroyed by Russian attacks - more than half of them this year alone,” Sybiha said on X.
He emphasized that the Ukrainian railway keeps the country moving. It enables the rapid evacuation of civilians from frontline areas, the transport of essential cargo, and the shipment of grain and other vital goods across the country.
“Amid daily attacks on our railway, it has become a key system for economic and social stability of the Ukrainian people and cities. To keep this lifeline running, Ukraine urgently needs replacements. We call on all our partners to urgently assist us in finding locomotives compatible with the 1520 mm gauge as well as in financing to accelerate the procurement of new ones. Supporting Ukraine’s railway resilience will help avert a humanitarian crisis and strengthen our resilience under the challenging conditions of full-scale war,” Sybiha urged, adding that supporting the resilience of the Ukrainian railway system would help prevent a humanitarian crisis and strengthen Ukraine's resilience amidst the challenging conditions of the full-scale war.
As reported, 209 locomotives belonging to JSC Ukrzaliznytsia were damaged as a result of Russian attacks throughout 2025 and the first quarter of 2026.
Before the war, in April 2021, the company operated 1,532 locomotives, comprising 749 electric and 783 diesel units. Held in reserve were 222 electric locomotives (109 freight and 113 passenger) and 223 diesel locomotives (66 for freight trains, seven for passenger service, and 150 shunting locomotives).

2 U.S. government workers accidentally shot by soldiers during anti-smuggling operation in Eswatini
Soldiers in the African nation of Eswatini accidentally shot two U.S. government personnel last week, the country's government said.
The U.S. personnel were shot during an anti-smuggling operation by the Eswatini army in a rural region in the northeast of the country late Friday, Eswatini's government said in a statement late Monday.
The Americans sustained "minor injuries" and there was an investigation underway, Eswatini government spokesperson Thabile Mdluli told The Associated Press on Tuesday.
The Eswatini government didn't immediately identify the U.S. personnel or say why they were present. The U.S. State Department said that it was aware of the shootings and the "affected U.S. personnel are safe," but also didn't immediately identify who they were. It said it was working with the Eswatini government on an investigation.
Army sources told Swaziland News that the soldiers accidentally shot a U.S. diplomat at a military roadblock. The sources told the outlet that soldiers were unaware that a car that made a U-turn next to a military roadblock was driven by an American diplomat and thought someone was illegally avoiding the roadblock.
Eswatini army spokesperson Sandile Gwebu told the AP that it was now "a diplomatic issue" handled by both countries and didn't give further details.
The Eswatini government said in its statement that "the incident is being treated with the seriousness it warrants."
Eswatini is a small kingdom of around 1.3 million people on the border between South Africa and Mozambique. It is ruled by King Mswati III, who holds supreme political power and is Africa's last absolute monarch.

Hungary’s purchases of Russian pipeline gas fall 12% in January-July
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
13:28:49 UTC
22:28:49 KST

MOSCOW, September 15. /TASS/. Hungary’s purchases of Russian pipeline gas fell by 12% in value terms between January and July 2026 as the country remained the leader among EU members in this regard, according to Eurostat data and TASS calculations.
The European Union imported Russian pipeline gas worth 512 mln euro in July. To date, the TurkStream gas pipeline remains the only active route for Russian gas supplies to Europe.
Hungary (171 mln euro), Bulgaria (119 mln euro), and Greece (132 mln euro) remained the leading purchasers. Slovakia purchased gas from Russia worth 90 mln euro.
In total, the European Union paid 3.4 bln euro for Russian pipeline gas between January and July compared to 3.6 bln euro in the previous year. The main buyers were Hungary (1.48 bln euro), which reduced its purchases by 11.8%, Bulgaria (822 mln euro), and Greece (671 mln euro).
TASS reported earlier that Russia increased gas exports to Europe via the TurkStream gas pipeline by 3.4% year-on-year to 10.25 bln cubic meters in January-July.

The National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) has charged a business partner of Ukrainian oligarch Ihor Kolomoisky in an alleged Hr 2.88 billion ($65 million) embezzlement scheme at state-controlled oil producer Ukrnafta, a law enforcement source told the Kyiv Independent on Sept. 15.
The NABU unveiled the investigation into the scheme on Sept. 15 but did not name the suspects.
The alleged ringleader is Mykhailo Kiperman, a co-owner of Kolomoisky’s Privat Group, according to the law enforcement source.
Other suspects include Yevhen Krychevskyi, a shareholder of several oil and gas companies linked to Kolomoisky; Feliks Lunyov, a former vice president at Ukrnafta, Bohdan Baradnyi, CEO of the Halychyna oil refinery, which was previously controlled by Kolomoisky, and Andriy Pinchuk, a deputy CEO of Ukrtatnafta, another company previously controlled by Kolomoisky, the source said.
They are accused of stealing 100,000 tonnes of oil products and laundering the proceeds.
The Kyiv Independent has requested comments from the suspects and will publish their responses once they are received.
Ukrnafta was co-owned by Kolomoisky's Privat Group and state-owned oil and gas company Naftogaz until 2022, when Kolomoisky's stake was nationalized under martial law during Russia's full-scale invasion.
Kolomoisky is currently on trial.
In 2023, Kolomoisky and his alleged accomplices were charged with embezzling $250 million from PrivatBank, the country's largest bank, which was nationalized in 2016 following alleged mismanagement by the oligarch.

Hospital could have prevented some of nurse's baby killings, judge says
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
13:27:42 UTC
22:27:42 KST

Some of nurse Lucy Letby's baby killings could have been prevented, U.K judge concludes: "Failure at all levels"
An English judge issued a scathing report Tuesday blaming dysfunctional management and a "complete failure at all levels" to protect babies at the hospital where neonatal nurse Lucy Letby was convicted of murdering seven newborns.
The inquiry into baby deaths found the Countess of Chester Hospital, in northwestern England, could have saved some infants from death and injury if staff had acted sooner when children began collapsing, Justice Kathryn Thirlwall said.
"Errors were made by nurses, doctors and managers," Thirlwall said. "There was also complete failure at all levels to invoke safeguarding procedures at any point."
The inquiry heard from more than 130 witnesses and considered 400 statements over six months, BBC News reported.
Letby, 36, is serving a life sentence for the murders of seven babies and attempted killing of seven others. She has maintained her innocence, and a defense team backed by dozens of scientists who have questioned the evidence against her are seeking to clear her name.
Thirlwall's inquiry did not review Letby's convictions but looked at how institutional failures exposed babies to repeatedly be harmed at the hospital and how staff and management responded and treated parents.
She focused on the failure of staff to intervene when it became clear someone was deliberately harming babies.
"How many lives could have been saved had the hospital acted differently?" she said. "It is clear that some babies would have been saved and some attacks would have been prevented if action was taken earlier."
Thirwall said the parents of babies were "kept in the dark for years" over concerns that their children may have been deliberately harmed, BBC News reported. Thirlwall found their treatment to be "reprehensible" and said hospital executives used the risk of upsetting the parents as a convenient argument to justify not calling the police.
Letby was convicted in 2023 of the murders of seven infants and attempted murders of six others — including two attempts on one child. A case in which jurors couldn't reach a decision was retried and Letby was convicted in July of another attempted murder. She was sentenced to 15 life terms with no chance of release. She is only the fourth woman in the United Kingdom to receive such a term.
"If all the babies whom [Letby] was convicted of murdering were removed from the annual number of deaths in the neonatal unit, the mortality figures would have been three in 2015 and three in 2016 — broadly consistent with previous years," Thirwall wrote, according to the BBC.
Prosecutors said Letby harmed babies in ways that left little trace, including injecting air into their bloodstreams, administering air or milk into their stomachs via nasogastric tubes, poisoning them with insulin and interfering with breathing tubes.
She was the only employee on duty in the neonatal unit when the children collapsed or died between June 2015 and June 2016. Prosecutors described her as a "constant malevolent presence."

Drone Strikes Force Half of Russia’s Top Diesel Refineries to Cut Output
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-15
13:27:08 UTC
22:27:08 KST

Half of Russia’s six largest diesel-producing refineries have been forced to significantly reduce or halt production this month after sustaining damage in Ukrainian drone attacks, according to Reuters calculations based on data from fuel market participants.
The disruption comes as Ukrainian strikes on Russia’s energy infrastructure continue to hit fuel production, prompting Moscow to restrict exports of gasoline, diesel and jet fuel.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
US President Donald Trump on Sunday called on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure, saying the strikes were causing a fuel shortage that was “hurting the world” – a concern he has pinned on Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries, rather than his own war in Iran.
Ukraine says Russian refineries are legitimate military targets.
Six refineries – Omsk, Kirishi, Taneco, Volgograd, NORSI and Perm – account for about half of Russia’s diesel production.
Kirishi has been fully shut down, while the Volgograd and NORSI refineries are operating at about one-quarter of their nameplate capacity.
Ukrainian strikes cripple Russian refining
Ukrainian drones have struck Russian oil refineries at least 70 times since the beginning of 2026, pushing Russia’s refining output to its lowest level in two decades.
By the end of August, gasoline production covered only around 70% of domestic demand, leaving a shortfall of roughly 30,000 tons per day.
Drone Attacks in the Ukrainian-Polish Border Region
At least 17 Russian regions have introduced restrictions on fuel sales, including limits of 30-40 liters per vehicle and “odd-even” systems based on license-plate numbers.
At least seven Russian refineries fully or partially halted production in August following drone attacks.
On Sept. 2, the KINEF refinery in Leningrad Oblast – Russia’s second-largest refinery by capacity – completely stopped processing.
Taneco was also hit on Sunday, although the full impact of the attack has not yet been assessed.
The disruptions have contributed to Moscow’s decision to restrict fuel exports. Before the restrictions, Russia exported less than 1 million metric tons of diesel in June, compared with around 2.5 million tons a year earlier. Including lower-quality gasoil, monthly exports had previously reached 3.3-3.4 million tons.
Turkey and Brazil were among the largest buyers, taking at least half of the available cargoes for several months before the restrictions were introduced.
The International Energy Agency said a Russian refinery was successfully hit, on average, once every three days during the first eight months of 2026.
The pressure on fuel markets is also being felt outside Russia. The US national average diesel price rose above $6 per gallon on Sept. 10 for the first time, according to GasBuddy.
Diesel is widely used to power trucks, trains, ships and agricultural machinery, making disruptions to supply particularly significant for transport and farming.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov claimed Monday that the war in Ukraine could have ended a year ago if the United States and Europe had not abandoned what he described as agreements reached at a 2025 summit in Alaska.

“That is an obvious fact, so draw your own conclusions,” Lavrov said, according to Russian state news agencies TASS and RIA Novosti and the Russian outlet RBC.

Lavrov said Moscow was open to both bilateral and trilateral negotiations. At the same time, he said Russia would not suspend its military operations against Ukraine while talks were underway.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and continues to occupy parts of the country. Moscow has repeatedly rejected calls for an unconditional ceasefire while demanding Ukrainian territorial concessions and restrictions on Kyiv’s military and foreign policy.

The Anchorage summit was promoted as an opportunity to advance efforts to end the conflict. Putin and Trump described the meeting as productive, but neither announced a ceasefire, peace framework or binding agreement afterward.

Pre-war status quo in Hormuz must be restored as soon as possible: Türkiye's Fidan
